question: Which of the following observations could NOT be explained by Rutherford’s model of the atom?

options.text: The stability of the atom despite the presence of accelerating electrons
The distribution of electrons around the nucleus
The presence of a positively charged nucleus in the atom
The deflection of alpha particles at large angles

solution:
The correct answer is __**1) The stability of the atom despite the presence of accelerating electrons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• **Rutherford’s atomic model** was based on the **gold foil experiment**, which demonstrated the existence of a **dense, positively charged nucleus** at the center of the atom surrounded by electrons.
 
• According to this model, electrons move around the nucleus in circular paths. However, **accelerating electrons** should theoretically emit electromagnetic radiation and lose energy over time.
 
• The stability of the atom cannot be explained by Rutherford’s model because, as electrons lose energy, they would spiral inward and collapse into the nucleus. This is inconsistent with the observation that atoms are stable. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
• **Statement 2:** Rutherford’s model did not provide details about how electrons are distributed or arranged around the nucleus. It only suggested that electrons revolve around the nucleus in circular paths. *Hence, statement 2 is correct.*
